get_user_by_external_id.description: Strongly-consistent GetItem on the UserUniquenessGuard item (pk EXT#<provider>#<external_id>, sk UNIQUE) to resolve user_id, then GetItem on USER#<user_id> / PROFILE for the profile; returns None if the guard item is absent.

revoke_all_user_sessions.description: Query all sessions for user via GSI1, then batch delete

delete_user.description: A patch that transitions status to Deleted writes the versioned User item (Put, conditioned on version) and removes the UserUniquenessGuard item (Delete, pk EXT#<provider>#<external_id> / sk UNIQUE) in the same transaction — both succeed or neither does. Removing the guard frees (provider, external_id) for re-registration: get_user_by_external_id returns None for the identity, and a later create_user for the same pair writes a fresh guard instead of losing to attribute_not_exists(pk). Any other update_user patch (no status change, or a change to Active/Suspended) stays a plain versioned PutItem and never touches the guard.

UserUniquenessGuard.description: Written in the same TransactWriteItems call as the User item, both conditioned on attribute_not_exists(pk), so a duplicate (provider, external_id) cancels the transaction with a Conflict instead of racing past an existing user. Removed in the same TransactWriteItems call as the versioned status write when a delete_user patch transitions the user to Deleted (see the delete_user access pattern), which is what frees (provider, external_id) for re-registration.
